## What I Do

I restructure code without changing behavior. I record a test baseline before touching anything, make structure-only edits, prove the same baseline stays green after, and check that I am removing duplication rather than adding a new near-duplicate.

## When To Use Me

- when behavior is already correct and only structure, naming, or duplication needs work
- before a review that must confirm behavior is unchanged
- when consolidating near-duplicate logic into a single source of truth
- when a smell is bounded to named files and no public contract should move

## Read Alongside

- `docs/ai/capabilities/verify-change/CAPABILITY.md`
- `docs/ai/capabilities/review-diff/CAPABILITY.md`
- `docs/ai/capabilities/docs-sync/CAPABILITY.md`
- `docs/ai/execution-protocol.md` (reference integrity, protect pre-existing changes)

## Steps

1. Confirm behavior is already correct and declare the scope contract: the exact files this refactor touches and the expected changed-file count.
2. Identify the covering tests and run them first to record a baseline (pass/fail/error counts, including any pre-existing failures). No baseline, no refactor.
3. Search for existing patterns and duplicate logic; if overlap is roughly >=75%, consolidate into the canonical location instead of adding a new abstraction.
4. Make the smallest structure-only change; keep mechanical moves (rename, extract, reorder) in separate passes from any semantic edit. Do not add features, change public contracts, or edit generated/lock/secret files.
5. Re-run the same tests and compare to the baseline: green must stay green; a green baseline requires zero new failures. Fix or revert within scope until it passes.
6. Report the refactor goal, the behavior-preservation boundary, the reuse check, and the before/after test counts, then hand off.

## Output

- the scope contract and behavior-preservation boundary
- structure changed and behavior confirmed unchanged
- the reuse/duplication check (what was searched, reused, and why any new code was needed)
- baseline and post-refactor test commands with pass/fail counts
- any behavior dimension you could not verify, marked explicitly as unverified rather than asserted equivalent

## Gotchas

- never claim green without an executed run; record baseline counts before editing
- the baseline must actually exercise the refactored behavior; passing-but-irrelevant tests are not proof of preservation
- preserve observable behavior: return values, errors/exceptions, side effects, output ordering, and public API/serialization shape
- a rename is a direct move, never a create+delete; do not delete files without explicit approval
- do not bundle unrelated refactors or weaken tests to make a change fit
- structural improvement is not a license to change an API or observable behavior
